entries.note: Wishing they were dead is hyperbole about potential losses. The embedded $4.65 trillion ownership estimate is separately checkable.

entries.test: Public financing and purchase records would show whether each discussed buyer except Microsoft raises tens of billions in debt to fund the GPU or TPU purchases.
entries.note: The condition is purchasing the hardware; no borrowing deadline is stated.

entries.test: CoreWeave disclosures, UBS's analysis, bond prices and contemporaneous market reporting would establish the stated financing exposure and whether its recognition drove the debt selloff.
entries.note: The principal claim explains an existing selloff; the three-year financing requirement is an embedded projection.

entries.test: Following an AI data center customer's inability to pay, public default records, capacity demand, vacancy and resale prices would show whether the predicted chain occurs.
entries.note: This asserts a firm conditional chain, rather than merely a possible risk.

entries.test: CoreWeave bond yields, construction progress and credit-market reporting would test the quoted yields and whether investor anxiety eases through any route other than accelerated construction.
entries.note: The record combines a current yield observation with an exclusive causal claim about restoring confidence.

entries.test: Amazon's quarterly filings and public reporting on rack deliveries, inventories and installation schedules would establish the capex, monthly deliveries and installation backlog.
entries.note: Zitron asserts the delivery pattern in his own voice, although the underlying email describes a projection.

entries.test: Public procurement records, supplier reporting and RAM and electronics price data would show whether NVIDIA's early-delivery pressure created shortages that increased those prices.
entries.note: The alleged purchasing pressure and price effects are observable conduct and outcomes.
The claim attributes an exclusive private motive to Huang. Sales and earnings data cannot establish that this was all he wanted.

entries.test: Anthropic's annual revenue and compute payments per megawatt, measured over the same period, would show whether costs above $20 million exceed the assumed revenue.
entries.note: This is a present accounting implication, not a future prediction. The annual basis comes from the surrounding Nomura discussion.

entries.test: Company disclosures, published analyst estimates and the labs' financing and compute expenditures would establish disclosure gaps, revenue concentration and dependence on fundraising.
entries.note: The proposition preserves the attribution of the 70% figure to analysts.

entries.test: Public estimates and disclosures of global AI compute purchases excluding OpenAI and Anthropic would establish whether spending is approximately $22 billion.
entries.note: An approximate numerical estimate remains checkable. Context identifies the spending as AI compute spending.

entries.test: Public customer-spending and unit-economics evidence would show whether most AI demand comes from services whose delivery costs exceed customer payments.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies a concrete reading: loss-making services subsidizing token use above subscription revenue.

entries.test: Venture investment allocations, portfolio returns relative to the S&P 500 and recipient-company financial results would test the claimed weak value creation and concentration in economically unproven LLM businesses.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraphs anchor value creation to investment returns and economic worth to business economics.
Neither 'work out' nor 'have a problem' defines a shared outcome threshold. The passage expresses a firm pessimistic outlook.

entries.test: Following further deterioration in AI debt markets, public financing terms, construction schedules and customer commitments would show whether operators borrow at 12%–15% for projects approximately three years away serving almost entirely the two labs.
entries.note: The three years describe the construction horizon; they do not set a deadline for the debt-market trigger.

entries.test: Anthropic's growth and contract disclosures, market movements and contemporaneous investor reporting would test whether concern about covering $413 billion in commitments drove the reaction and whether valuations depend on continued growth.
entries.note: The normalized claim retains an asserted causal explanation without adopting the separate claim about what everybody privately knows.
Bailing out missed expectations or investor sentiment has no agreed operational meaning. This does not specify a fiscal limit or a concrete intervention whose success could settle it.

entries.test: Public reporting on whether OpenAI closes the $30 billion round at a $1.4 trillion valuation, including delays, investor resistance or revised terms, would test the predicted fundraising difficulty.
entries.note: The fundraising prediction is firm and checkable. The conditional survival remark expresses uncertainty rather than a firm prediction of failure.
